metadata.title: Redefining Processing Efficiency with In-Memory Computing Architecture
metadata.description: In-memory computing offers a transformative solution to address the bottlenecks of conventional computing architectures, were frequent data transfer between memory and processors limits performance. This study presents the design and evaluation of an in-memory computing architecture aimed at significantly reducing latency, enhancing energy efficiency, and increasing throughput by performing computations directly within memory arrays. By embedding logic functions alongside memory components, the proposed architecture achieves notable improvements in computational efficiency. Experimental results reveal that the architecture reduces latency by up to 43.33%, with tasks such as matrix multiplication demonstrating a decrease from 450 microseconds to 275 microseconds. Energy consumption is reduced by over 40%, as evidenced by neural network inference requiring only 7.2 joules compared to 12.5 joules in baseline systems. Furthermore, architecture enhances throughput by up to 52%, with AI model training achieving 1,520,000 operations per second compared to 1,000,000 in traditional architectures. These results establish the potential of in-memory computing to redefine conventional processing paradigms, delivering high-speed, energy-efficient computations for applications in AI, machine learning, and other data-intensive domains.

metadata.title: GDP per Energy Use at the Global Level
metadata.description: The variable "GDP/unit of energy use" measures the economic efficiency of a country or region's energy use. In other words, it represents the economic value generated per unit of energy consumed. This metric is calculated as the ratio of GDP to total energy consumption. The formula to calculate "GDP/unit of energy use" is: GDP per unit of energy use = GDP / Energy Consumption. Where: GDP is the total value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period, usually expressed in US dollars or another local currency; Energy Consumption is the total amount of energy used, expressed in units such as Joules, Terajoules, or equivalents in tons of oil (toe). This indicator is useful for assessing how efficiently an economy uses energy to produce economic value. A higher "GDP/unit of energy use" value indicates greater energy efficiency, as more economic value is produced per unit of energy consumed.

metadata.title: Design and implementation of 4-quadrant chopper for speed control of EVs and regenerative braking analysis
metadata.description: This paper presents a novel 4-quadrant chopper design for controlling the speed of electric vehicles, featuring a regenerative braking mechanism to improve energy efficiency. Regenerative braking recovers energy during deceleration by converting kinetic energy into electrical energy stored in the battery. This process activates automatically when the accelerator pedal is released, slowing the vehicle while reducing reliance on mechanical brakes, which remain available for emergency situations. The system’s voltage control is achieved using a pulse-width modulation (PWM) technique that adjusts the duty cycle of switching devices. A microcontroller serves as the system’s core, generating PWM signals and coordinating its operation. The performance of the chopper was evaluated through simulations and experiments, demonstrating that optimal energy recovery occurs at duty cycles of 55-65%. The results revealed that up to 400 joules of energy can be regenerated per braking cycle, particularly in stop-start driving conditions. This innovative design contributes to a 5-10% extension in battery life per charge cycle, enhancing the overall efficiency and sustainability of electric vehicles. The proposed system demonstrates significant potential for energy recovery and reduced wear on mechanical braking systems, paving the way for more efficient electric vehicle technologies.

metadata.title: Technical and social innovation actions in social housing: a pilot case in the South of Italy
metadata.description:
Abstract: Energy efficiency retrofitting of public social housing is a key challenge for a more sustainable and inclusive society, alleviating energy poverty, increasing living conditions and indoor comfort quality of vulnerable households, improving dwellings and neighbourhoods. However, every action should be inspired by a “people-centric” 
approach. Within REHOUSE, Renovation packagEs for HOlistic improvement of EU’s bUildingS Efficiency, maximizing RES generation and cost-effectiveness”, Horizon 
Europe, ENEA coordinates a pilot case in Italy, in Apulia Region. Interventions on social housing will address both the active and passive components of the building leading to the improvement of the envelope insulation level, while locally producing RES electricity from the Building integrated Photovoltaic Panels located in favourably-oriented façades. PV will be coupled to renovated active energy supply based on the central heat pump, Biobased PCM storage. It is crucial that innovative technological solutions installation is based on occupants’ acceptance, including co-design elements, since end-users and even those stakeholders not used to participate in research/innovation projects become an integral part of the process. Households have been engaged since the beginning of the prototype specifications, through social requisites elicitation, and thanks to a social task force.

The methodology has started from a mutual understanding, with interviews and questionnaires, this operation was carried out by experiences and surveys in presence and 
proximity (ethnographic approach). A bottom-up approach aims at achieving new behaviours in the future renovated dwellings. Therefore, starting from an empirical 
analysis of users’ needs we have acquired useful information to reach high level of acceptance of innovations.

metadata.title: Straw supply costs for Germany – NUTS3 | 2010-2020 | farm-side
metadata.description: The dataset contains information on the supply costs of cereal straw in Germany from 2010-2020 at NUTS 3 (county) level. The supply costs depend on the specific straw yield in each NUTS region and the assumed underlying supply chain. The specific straw yield is the NUTS specific average of the most relevant cereals [wheat, rye, oats, triticale, spring barley, winter barley] The supply chain is defined according to the NUTS specific average farm area in relation to the national average. Supply costs are divided into collection costs, transport costs, storage costs and opportunity costs. Opportunity costs are defined as the monetary cost of replacing the nutrients removed. The connecting research paper, which describes the methodology in detail is available under this DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s12649-024-02528-x.

metadata.title: Synthesis and outcome from the household engagement programmes in seven European countries, updated
metadata.description: This report “Synthesis and outcome from the household engagement programmes in seven European countries, updated” serves a crucial purpose in providing a comprehensive understanding of the household energy engagement programmes implemented with energy poor households across seven diverse countries. Through a comparative analysis and synthesis of outcomes from local actions, the report delves into the intricate dynamics shaped by socio-political contexts, socio-demographic profiles, and cultural specificities in each locale. The emphasis on multiple countries and their associated socio-demographic contexts, including lower-income occupants of multi-family buildings, enriches the depth of insights. Drawing on data regarding energy usage and behaviour change, the report evaluates the effectiveness of the methods employed in promoting behavioural shifts and extracts valuable lessons for further development. By identifying critical aspects, challenges, and successes, the report lays out the different stages of the EnergyMeasures activities and where recommendations for supporting the replication of best practices should be prioritised. In essence, this report not only consolidates the accomplishments and learnings from the implemented programmes but also serves as a guiding document for future endeavours in addressing energy poverty through targeted engagement strategies.

metadata.title: Replication of household energy engagement programmes
metadata.description: The present report uses the analysis undertaken under the Synthesis and outcome from the household engagement programmes to develop a replication plan detailing the potential means of transferring the knowledge gained in seven local actions and replicating their best practices elsewhere. The objective of the replication plan is to support energy poverty advocacy organisations and other stakeholders to devise and implement tailored household energy engagement programmes in other areas. The replication plan will be prepared through a process of co-production involved all key stakeholders involved in the actions. The resultant document will comprise a step-by-step guide for the implementation of the methodology – including guidance on selecting socio-cultural appropriate behaviour change methods, expected results – along with supporting materials.
